finding.claim: The user-supplied icon URL is stored without any validation and later fetched server-side by the nightly sync job. An attacker can set it to an internal or cloud-metadata URL such as http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/ or an internal service, and the server will issue a GET to it. The response is read as a byte array, so it can be used to read the response or probe internal hosts. The scheme and host are completely unrestricted. Java's HttpClient only supports http and https, and does not follow redirects by default, but this does not prevent http/https access to internal targets.
finding.source: The `icon` parameter of Profile.update, handled by PUT /profile (line 11), which is attacker-controlled.

trace.note: PUT /profile calls update(webhook, icon). The `icon` parameter is user input.
this.iconUrl = icon stores the value with no scheme, host or IP validation. Only `webhook` is checked, at line 12.
The nightly sync job runs with a privileged network position.
URI.create(iconUrl) is passed to HttpClient.send as a GET, and the response is read with BodyHandlers.ofByteArray().

finding.guards_checked: The regex check at line 12 applies only to `webhook`, not `icon`. There is no scheme allowlist, host allowlist, resolved-IP check, or egress filtering visible in the code. The HttpClient is passed in, so its configuration is not visible; Java's HttpClient does not follow redirects by default. The webhookUrl sink at line 21 is not reported as a finding: its full-match regex pins the scheme and host to https://hooks.example.com/ followed by 20 alphanumerics, so the attacker cannot influence the host (matches() anchors the whole string, and there is no userinfo, @, or backslash to confuse the parser).

verdict.reason: src/Profile.java:16 stores `icon` unvalidated (the regex at line 12 covers only `webhook`), and sync() at lines 23-24 sends a GET to URI.create(iconUrl) with no scheme or host restriction. The "privileged network position" note on line 20 is an inference, not something the code shows, but it doesn't change the result.
